correctness.rationale: The independent covariance integrals give C_n(t)=t(1-t^n)/(n+1) and V_n=n²/[(n+1)²(2n+1)]. Gaussian projection yields risk; derivative sign is an explicit degree-(n+2) polynomial. By Descartes plus known signs it has one interior simple root for all eta>0, and the factored eta=0 case has one interior root. Noise ordering and three information asymptotics follow from the exact critical-point balance and uniqueness of the positive exponential root. Exact rational checks (322) and >48000 high-precision comparisons support but are not replacements for these arguments. Boundary cases n=1, eta=0 and t∈{0,1} explicitly handled.

value.rationale: The normalized Beta(n,1) family is a canonical endpoint-concentrating sequence of polynomial integral functionals in Brownian approximation, not an arbitrarily chosen one-off weight. The theorem resolves a natural one-measurement sensor-design decision for all integer n and eta, with a nontrivial singular noncommutation between fixed positive noise and high polynomial order; it quantifies a new high-order information-collapse and exact n*eta crossover for path-integral sensing, rather than simply computing a known covariance.
